Getting rid of a Gmail account. One step forward. Using a Android app for email account access. Two steps backwards...

ProtonMail is probably the best free alternative (if you're looking for something more "secure", which I'm assuming you are since Gmail would probably be just fine otherwise).

Pros:
- For privacy: it is open-source, has end-to-end encryption, doesn't require or track personal info, and for what it's worth it is based in Switzerland.
- It has a good UI.
- It's a good sized company so it stays updated, is more likely to implement more good features in the future, and is less likely to flop.
- You can abbreviate your email as xxxxx@pm.me which is quite useful since it is simple and easy to remember, and people won't typically recognize a domain that isn't one of the popular ones.
Cons: - It doesn't encrypt the header.
- Its App is meh. It isn't open source, and it's dependent on having Google Play for notifications if you run Android (which is silly since one of their biggest selling points is that they're "not Google").
- No search function (this is one of the most important functions in a personal email imho). Although this you can apparently bypass if you use ProtonMail Bridge?

Other alternatives to consider: I've heard plenty of good things about Tutanota which seems about on par with ProtonMail (so might be worth looking into). There's also Scryptmail, Posteo (which is a paid service though), OpenMailbox, Fastmail, and no doubt some others which I have heard of but haven't looked into.
Another option is to create your own, if you're feeling ambitious. Even if you don't have the expertise to do it all yourself, I believe there are Wordpress-like things that provide tools & a framework to do it yourself. Don't have much experience with this route, but it's another option to consider if you're a go-getter.

Unfortunately there's no one best service. They all have various flaws, like protonmail engaged in political censorship for instance. Lavabit seemed legit as the owner actually shut it down rather than give anything to the feds. I bet 90%+ of other services will immediately buckle to government demands for anything to avoid being shut down.

If you just want convenience/all-in-one, just pick something like tutanoa. It's better than Gmail, as literally anything is better than giving Google more information about you.
